title: Verifier-assisted evaluation of LLM-generated network configurations for deterministic reachability and isolation
research_question: When asked to translate high-level network intent into device-level configurations, how reliably do current LLMs produce configurations that satisfy deterministic operational properties (reachability, isolation, ACL policy compliance) as measured by a formal network verifier, and how much does an explicit generate–validate–repair pipeline improve that reliability?
confirmatory_hypotheses: LLM-generated configurations produced in a single-shot prompt will fail verifier-checked reachability/isolation properties on a substantial fraction (>20%) of tasks in the public synthetic topology/policy corpus.

A generate–validate–repair pipeline that uses a deterministic verifier to identify failures and requests targeted repairs from the LLM will significantly increase the fraction of verifier-passing configurations compared to single-shot generation (absolute increase >10 percentage points).
exploratory_questions: How much marginal utility (absolute pass-rate improvement) is obtained per repair iteration (up to three iterations)?
Which strata (topology size, policy class) show the largest/smallest repair success rates?
What is the median and distribution of model calls required per successful repair (cost-per-success)?
Do automated contamination-detection signals (n-gram overlap / exact-line matches) predict unusually high pass rates (possible leakage)?
benchmark_scope: Public synthetic corpus (published alongside study artifacts) pairing realistic topologies, device templates, and intent→policy pairs (see provenance & release plan below).
Reference to prior public evaluation corpora (NetConfEval-like public corpora) for scope alignment and comparison.
model_scope: Single hosted LLM provider accessible via API (hosted_model_api_available). Exact model identifier and model-version will be recorded and frozen at experiment start and reported in the Disclosure Statement (execution-time record).
Use of a single model avoids multi-model generalization claims; results are explicitly bounded to the chosen hosted model.
transformation_scope: Automated parsing and canonicalization of LLM textual outputs into verifier-input device configs using deterministic parsers and canonicalizers developed in the repo.
Verifier assertions: deterministic reachability, isolation, and ACL compliance checks executable on canonicalized configs.
primary_estimand: Per-task difference in verifier pass indicator (pipeline-after-up-to-3-iterations) minus single-shot baseline pass indicator (paired proportion difference).
secondary_estimands: Per-iteration marginal increase in pass probability (iteration 1, iteration 2, iteration 3).
Median model calls per successful repair.
Stratum-specific pass rates (small/medium/large topologies; policy classes).
sampling_plan: Confirmatory sample: N=240 tasks drawn from the public synthetic corpus, stratified equally across three topology-size strata (small/medium/large): 80 tasks per stratum. An additional exploratory holdout set of 60 tasks (same strata distribution) will be reserved for exploratory analyses and robustness checks. Inclusion: tasks with well-formed intent→policy pairs and canonical device templates. Exclusion: tasks whose synthetic topology or device templates fail automated schema validation (parser stage) prior to prompting; such exclusions are deterministic and logged. Total confirmatory tasks = 240; discovery (exploratory) tasks = 60. Rationale and derivation: see Power Plan below.
analysis_plan: Primary analysis is paired: per-task baseline vs final-pipeline verifier pass. Use McNemar's test (binomial paired discordant test) to test the confirmatory hypothesis (alpha=0.05, two-sided). Report absolute difference, 95% CI (exact binomial or nonparametric bootstrap), p-value, and effect-size. Report marginal utility per iteration (paired difference after iteration k vs iteration k-1). Stratified descriptive statistics for pre-defined strata (80 tasks each). Exploratory subgroup comparisons are labeled exploratory; multiplicity correction (Bonferroni) applied when presenting secondary confirmatory-sounding claims; otherwise report uncorrected results with explicit exploratory labeling.
multiplicity_plan: One pre-registered primary outcome (paired verifier pass-rate difference). All other analyses (iteration marginals, strata) are exploratory except pre-specified stratified descriptive reporting. When multiple hypothesis tests are reported beyond the primary test, apply Bonferroni correction across the named secondary tests or label them as exploratory with unadjusted p-values.
missingness_plan: Technical model/API failures: automatically retry up to 2 technical retries (total 3 attempts per call) with exponential backoff. If still failing, mark the task-call as 'technical failure' and exclude from the primary paired analysis (primary analysis set requires both baseline and pipeline endpoints available). Sensitivity analyses: treat missing baseline or pipeline outputs conservatively as verifier-fail in an alternate ITT-style sensitivity analysis. All exclusions, counts, and reasons are logged deterministically and included in results tables.

benchmark_names: Public synthetic topology/policy corpus (this study; will be released with provenance)
risk_factors: Training-data leakage (model memorization of publicly shared config fragments).
High verbatim overlap between synthetic corpus templates and model pretraining data.
detection_procedures: Automated exact-line matching: compute SHA256 hashes per canonical config line and detect exact-line reuse between synthetic corpus and model-generated configs.
N-gram overlap scoring: compute normalized n-gram (n=5) overlap between each generated config and every corpus config; record overlap score.
High-similarity fingerprinting: Jaccard on token-level shingles; flag items with overlap above pre-specified thresholds.
item_flagging_rules: Flag as 'possible-contamination' when exact-line match count ≥ 2 lines or normalized 5-gram overlap > 0.30 (30%).
Flag as 'likely-contamination' when exact-line match count ≥ 5 lines or normalized 5-gram overlap > 0.60.
contamination_plan.analysis_treatment: Report pass rates separately for flagged vs non-flagged tasks. Primary confirmatory analysis excludes flagged items from contamination sensitivity analysis only if pre-registered threshold crossed; otherwise include all items and report contamination-stratified results. All flagged items are included in the public artifact with flags so readers can reproduce alternate treatments.
residual_uncertainty: Automated overlap detection may miss semantic memorization where the model produces functionally equivalent but token-different configs.
Thresholds chosen are conservative but partially arbitrary; sensitivity across thresholds will be reported.

budget_scenarios.description: Conservative / low-cost: confirmatory N=120 (40 per stratum), single-shot baseline + at most 1 repair iteration for failing cases, strict per-task call cap = 2. Intended when provider rate or cost constraints bind.
models: Single hosted LLM API (model id to be recorded at execution start)
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Per-task max calls 2 leads to per-task worst-case 240 calls; baseline 120 + estimated repair calls (assume 30% fail→36 repairs) = 156; add 20% overhead for retries/logging → ~187 → rounded to 200 planned calls. Well within the manifest model-call cap (10000).

budget_scenarios.description: Recommended balanced scenario: confirmatory N=240 (80 small / 80 medium / 80 large), baseline single-shot + up to 3 repair iterations for failing cases, per-task call cap = 4 (1 baseline + 3 repairs). Provides adequate power and stratified inference while remaining low-cost.
models: Single hosted LLM API (model id to be recorded at execution start)
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Worst-case per-task calls = 4 → max possible calls = 240*4 = 960. Empirically expected calls: baseline 240 + repair calls estimated from 30% baseline fail rate (72 failing tasks) × mean 2 repair iterations ≈ 144 → total ≈ 384; add 20% overhead for retries/logging → ≈ 461 → rounded to 500 planned calls. This is below the platform model-call cap (10000) and fits within the 7-day wall-clock execution window using CPU verifier runs and hosted-model latency assumptions.

budget_scenarios.description: Generous / high-powered: confirmatory N=400, baseline + up to 3 repair iterations, per-task cap = 4. For use if budget and rate-limits permit larger sample and more precise stratum estimates.
models: Single hosted LLM API (model id to be recorded at execution start)
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Worst-case calls = 400*4 = 1600. Expected call estimate (30% fail rate × avg 2 repair iterations) gives ~640, overhead → ~800 planned calls. Still below platform cap (10000) but larger wall-clock/time cost; included as optional if sponsor resources permit.

power_plan.primary_estimand: Paired difference in verifier pass probability (pipeline_after_repairs − single_shot_baseline).
power_plan.target_effect: Absolute increase of 10 percentage points (0.10) in pass probability (pipeline vs baseline).
power_plan.clustering_unit: Task (intent→topology instance); paired within-task comparison between baseline and pipeline outputs.
power_plan.calculation_method: McNemar-style paired binary outcome sample-size rationale: approximate sample size n = (Z_{alpha/2}+Z_{beta})^2 * (p01 + p10) / delta^2 where p01 and p10 are discordant proportions. With alpha=0.05 (Z=1.96), power 0.80 (Z_beta=0.84), assumed discordant sum (p01+p10) ≈ 0.20 (conservative for 10% absolute change), the formula yields n≈157. To allow stratified analyses, buffer for lower-than-expected discordance, and deterministic exclusions, we pre-register N=240 confirmatory tasks (80 per stratum).
assumptions: Baseline pass rate ≈ 70% (baseline fail ≈ 30%) motivated by literature and pilot signals; actual rates may differ but the chosen N=240 provides margin.
Discordant-pair sum p01+p10 assumed ≈ 0.20 for sample-size calculation; sensitivity analysis will be reported for p01+p10 in [0.15,0.30].
Paired design maintained by evaluating baseline and pipeline for every task; missingness handled by deterministic retry policy and sensitivity analysis.
power_plan.minimum_detectable_effect_notes: With N=240 and assumed discordant sum 0.20, the detectable absolute paired difference (two-sided, power 0.8) is ≈0.07–0.10 depending on actual discordant sum; we pre-register the 10-percentage-point target and will report achieved minimum detectable effect given observed discordant counts.
sensitivity_analyses: Recompute achieved power and minimum detectable effect conditional on observed discordant counts (p01+p10).
Repeat primary analysis treating missing API outputs as failures (conservative ITT sensitivity).
Report results across reduced samples (per-stratum N=80) and pooled N.

transformation_families: Syntax parsing and canonicalization of textual device configs into verifier input format.
Deterministic template instantiation and variable binding.
semantic_equivalence_checks: Round-trip check: parse(L->canonical)->pretty-print and re-parse to confirm idempotence; verifier-consistency check: run verifier on both original-L and canonicalized config to ensure identical assertions.
Unit tests with canonical examples (canonical positive/negative cases) to ensure verifier semantics match specification.
automatic_rejection_rules: If parser fails deterministically for an LLM output, mark that output as 'parse-fail' and count as verifier-fail for that iteration; log exact parser error.
If canonicalization changes more than 10% of non-whitespace tokens relative to original output (indicative of major re-formatting), flag and count as parser-fail for that iteration.
transformation_validation.audit_sample_policy: Every 50th generated configuration (per scenario) is subjected to an expanded automated audit consisting of (a) line-hash comparison against corpus, (b) additional syntactic validators, (c) run-time verifier stress test. All audit checks are automated and deterministic; results are logged and published.
transformation_validation.mapping_validation: Canonicalizer and verifier come with a unit test suite (≥100 canonical positive/negative cases) executed before experiment run; tests are recorded with hashes. Any failing test halts execution until automated-fix or code update is applied and re-tested; such halts and fixes are logged and reported.
residual_risks: Parser corner-cases that require human-intelligible repair cannot be addressed by the automated pipeline; those cases will be counted and reported as parse-failures.
Semantic-equivalence heuristics may not capture certain vendor-specific idiosyncrasies; these are discussed as noncritical external-validity limits.

remaining_noncritical_uncertainties: External validity: synthetic public corpora may not capture full production heterogeneity (multivendor idiosyncrasies); conclusions are explicitly bounded to the public synthetic corpus and the chosen hosted model.
Hosted-model nondeterminism: unavoidable variability in model outputs remains; handled via retries, per-task paired design, and sensitivity analyses but residual sampling noise is noncritical.
Contamination detection is automated (n-gram/line-match) but cannot prove absence of semantic memorization; treated as residual uncertainty and reported via sensitivity stratification.

Exact model identifier and any provider-side metadata (randomness seeds, temperature internals) will be recorded at execution start—until then some provider internals are unavailable but this does not block execution as the capability manifest permits hosted-model API use.
